title: A cut between two clips rolls to the playhead from its right-click
goal: Right-clicking a cut inside one clip offers Roll Edit to Playhead, but right-clicking the cut where two separate clips meet offers only transitions, though on the timeline the two cuts look the same. An editor used to Premiere expects to roll any edit point. Give the cut between two clips the same roll, so the outgoing clip gets longer by exactly what the incoming one gives up and nothing after it moves.
notes: Manager pass 2026-10-05, from reading the code, not yet seen on screen (hence p2 and the reproduce step). EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift:432-457 timelineCutMenuRows (a join inside one clip) ends with Roll Edit to Playhead via rollClipCut; timelineEditPointMenuRows (:461-479, the point between two clips, TimelineEditPoint outgoing/incoming) returns only Apply Default / Add / Remove Transition. The right-click task (right-click-does-what-you-would-expect-everywher, audit 2026-09-23-right-click-menus.json) built the roll for joins before edit points between separate clips existed (bring-in-a-second-clip-and-cut-between-clips, ClipLanding.swift). Spare footage between clips: DocumentCut / documentCut(at:) already reports spare for transitions; reuse it.
